title: Canonical coordinates for composition model orientations
statement: Fix a finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions]. Use its finite constant coefficient category and the recorded exact site comparison. For a scheme X and rank r define the shifted Tate power T_r=Lambda_X(r)[2r]. Define its ordered multiplication, canonical pullback, and their composite mu. Express the specified diagonal orientation in the tensor-mate coefficient-unit coordinates by applying the exceptional functor to the canonical coefficient-unit isomorphism. For the fixed affine coordinate model, define ordered Gamma from chartGamma at each positive finite level and the coordinate morphism reversing the finite coordinate order into the iterated affine-line model. Define a model Gamma family, its prescribed-coordinate normalization and its rank-zero normalization. Define b_r by pulling the inverse Gamma along the zero section and then applying Tate restriction. Define the base-changed q orientation and total affine orientation, and their affine and zero-section multiplication equations. On a composable affine smooth pair, define the beta-delta equation and the three beta identifications in actual conormal frames. Finally define the shift-removed Tate object, its concentration/rank-one/automorphism-detection predicate, source normalization and naturality, and the conjunction of these predicates with the global orientation and quotient equations. All objects, maps and predicates are the unchanged definitions previously accompanying lem-pur-composition-model-orientation-descent.
